paragraphs.source_en: Still as stone, she thought. She sat unmoving. The cut was quick, the blade sharp. By rights the metal should have been cold against her flesh, but it felt warm instead. She could feel the blood washing down her face, a rippling red curtain falling across her brow and cheeks and chin, and she understood why the priest had made her close her eyes. When it reached her lips the taste was salt and copper. She licked at it and shivered.

paragraphs.source_en: “Bring me the face,” said the kindly man. The waif made no answer, but she could hear her slippers whispering over the stone floor. To the girl he said, “Drink this,” and pressed a cup into her hand. She drank it down at once. It was very tart, like biting into a lemon. A thousand years ago, she had known a girl who loved lemon cakes.

units.source_en: The girl took a deep shuddering breath, and realized it was true.
No one was choking her, no one was hitting her.
Even so, her hand was shaking as she raised it to her face.

She felt her cheeks, touched her eyes, traced the line of her jaw.
“My face is still the same.”

Are you certain?”
